summary: Attempt-2 correction round is independently verified. The full git diff against HEAD corresponds only to task 11.1 (9 modified tracked files: PLANS.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/changelog.md, docs/data-model.md, docs/implementation-readiness.md, docs/limitations.md, docs/project-status.md, src/ArrTags/Configuration/OperationalLimits.cs, src/ArrTags/Configuration/config.html; plus 4 new untracked cache source files, 1 new untracked test file, and the docs/implementation/11.1/ reports). No unrelated change, no provider-client/reader/invalidation wiring, and no ETag/revision-token/history-since/SignalR dependency was introduced. I rebuilt (0 warnings/0 errors) and re-ran the tests: focused ArrInventoryCacheTests 24/24 passed; full default suite Failed 0, Passed 1387, Skipped 63, Total 1450, matching the worker's reported counts. I independently reproduced sensitivity with three throwaway mutations: (1) breaking ArrInventoryCache.FromLimits (wrong TTL unit and swapped record/byte fields) fails FromLimitsBindsTheValidatedLimitsToTheCache; (2) making TryStore advance observedAt when lastError is non-null fails ProviderFailureRetainedThroughTheCacheBoundaryNeverExtendsTheWindow; (3) adding an ArrConnection-typed member to ArrInventoryCacheEntry fails InventoryCacheTypesExposeNoCredentialBearingMembers. All three mutations were reverted and the tree re-verified green. All attempt-1 HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW test-quality findings (TQ-11.1-1..6) are genuinely closed, and SEC-11.1-3 is closed; SEC-11.1-1 is resolved for 11.1 by honest documentation that matches the actual guarantee (boundary value-level redaction is explicitly stated as a producer contract, not a boundary enforcement), with enforcement carried into 11.2 as the security reviewer itself recommended. All five acceptance criteria still hold and the documented limits match the code. No required changes.

attempt1_finding_disposition.note: New FromLimitsBindsTheValidatedLimitsToTheCache uses distinctive non-default values (90 min, 7 records, 3 MiB) and asserts Ttl == TimeSpan.FromMinutes(90), MaxRecordsPerConnection == 7, MaxBytesPerConnection == 3 MiB plus the default mapping. Independently mutation-tested: swapping record/byte fields and using TimeSpan.FromSeconds fails the test (Failed 1 / Passed 23).

New ProviderFailureRetainedThroughTheCacheBoundaryNeverExtendsTheWindow drives TryStore(..., lastError:) and asserts the failure-annotated entry is retrievable, its LastError is the same reference, and ObservedAt/ExpiresAt/StaleUntil are identical to a clean store at the same observedAt/TTL, with records preserved and eviction at now >= StaleUntil. Independently mutation-tested: advancing observedAt inside TryStore when lastError is non-null fails the test (Failed 1 / Passed 23). The entry-level WithFailure test also now asserts record preservation.

The name heuristic is renamed InventoryCacheTypesHaveNoSecretNamedMembers and explicitly marked secondary; a new structural InventoryCacheTypesExposeNoCredentialBearingMembers scans the member types (unwrapping generics/arrays) of all four model types against a denylist (ArrConnection, ArrConnectionConfiguration, SecretReference, SecretLease, PluginConfiguration, MetadataStateEntry, MetadataStateStore) and is non-vacuous (Assert.True(inspected > 0)). Independently mutation-tested: adding an ArrConnection-typed member fails it (Failed 1 / Passed 23). A new LastErrorSatisfiesTheBoundedRedactedProviderErrorContract asserts the message is bounded to MaxMessageLength and ArrProviderError exposes exactly Code/Retryability/Message.

New ByteBoundIsEnforcedAtTheActualEntrySize uses the entry's real SizeBytes: accepted at maxBytes == SizeBytes and rejected at maxBytes == SizeBytes - 1, so the byte check is exercised at the actual accounting boundary rather than an always-too-small bound.

Renamed to OverBoundObservationSetIsRejectedWithoutDisplacingTheRetainedSet and now asserts the observable contract: an over-record store returns false, Count stays 1, and the previously retained single-record set is still returned; the over-byte store leaves Count 0.

The near-tautological IsAssignableFrom asserts are removed. InventoryCacheEntryIsDistinctFromThePerItemMetadataStateRecord keeps the JellyfinItemId/MatchStatus/Metadata property-absence checks and now scans the member types of ArrInventoryCacheEntry and ArrInventoryCache (non-vacuously) and asserts neither references MetadataStateEntry or MetadataStateStore.

No new redaction policy was invented and production behavior is unchanged. The ArrInventoryCache/ArrInventoryCacheEntry remarks, docs/data-model.md section 6, and docs/architecture.md section 12 now state that the entry's only free-text carrier is a bounded ArrProviderError and that value-level redaction of that message is the producer contract (ArrProviderError is documented as bounded and redacted, ADR-020 clause 4), consistent with MetadataStateEntry.LastError, and that the boundary does not redact it. The non-secret caller contract is documented on TryStore's lastError parameter. This matches the actual guarantee and does not overstate it. Boundary-level sanitization remains the security reviewer's pre-11.2 recommendation and is disclosed as a known limitation; it is not a 11.1 acceptance defect.

Addressed by the structural member-type denylist (TQ-11.1-3) and by phrasing the secret-free claim as backed by the canonical-type/structural guard rather than the name heuristic, which is now labelled secondary.

findings.summary: The 'consistent with the per-item metadata record's last-error summary' wording compares an ArrProviderError? carrier to MetadataStateEntry.LastError, which is a bounded string?.
findings.detail: MetadataStateEntry.LastError is declared as string? (src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/MetadataStateEntry.cs:273), whereas ArrInventoryCacheEntry.LastError is ArrProviderError?. The documentation analogy is at the contract level (a bounded, non-secret failure summary), not the type level, and the security-reviewer's own assessment used the same comparison. No correctness impact; the wording is not misleading in context.

findings.detail: SEC-11.1-1's enforcement half (sanitize ArrProviderError.Message at the cache boundary) was not implemented.
